projects.name: zcoms
projects.description: A scriptable command-line comms platform (the zc binary) that drives Telegram (TDLib), WhatsApp (Baileys), and Instagram from the terminal, with an AI agent layer that orchestrates LLM-backed agents (Claude/Codex) directly from the owner's chats. The agent tier runs a role-separated multi-agent pipeline — an Interviewer collects information, a Guard screens it for prompt-injection and unsafe content, and a Producer builds and delivers the result — alongside triage, scheduling, and per-persona prompt management. It grew into a layered ecosystem around local IPC sockets, adding team coordination, an Angular admin console, and a Telegram Stars commerce platform, with tiers communicating only through published Go client packages.

frontend: In-house ui component library (consumed via file:libs/ui)
Compiled and embedded into the Go binary via go:embed
other: LLM backend abstraction (Claude Code / Codex CLIs)
Prompt engineering (per-persona seeds + dynamic context injection)
Prompt-injection guardrails (Guard agent + store-guard permission model)

Designed and built the entire multi-tier comms and commerce ecosystem
Owned the TDLib session, WhatsApp sidecar integration, and IPC protocol
Engineered prompt-injection guardrails across the agent pipeline and data stores
Built and maintained release packaging and deployment tooling

Implemented an LLM backend abstraction supporting Claude Code and Codex CLIs with per-task backend routing, turn timeouts, and bounded output capture

projects.name: VerifyPortal
projects.description: A document data-extraction and verification portal where users upload documents, an OCR pipeline extracts structured data against configurable presets, and results are returned through a web UI or a public agent API. The backend follows Clean Architecture with CQRS, and public sign-up is gated behind an allowlist pending payment-provider integration.

projects.name: invites.blog
projects.description: A premium animated digital-invitation platform where inviters create personalized, role-aware invites without an account and invitees open a unique link to RSVP with zero login. It uses a manifest-driven template system so new template fields render automatically without code changes, with strong privacy guarantees (possession tokens, only hashed token storage, sandboxed invitee rendering). Mid-development it pivoted to a made-to-order bespoke inquiry pipeline (inquire, design, refine, deliver).

projects.name: MOTCA Domain
